I love music. I love it because all the problems and issues in the world just go away when I'm playing. It's almost like my brain stops thinking in words for a minute and thinks in notes and rhythms instead. Very relaxing.
I too share this outlook. I'm a musician of 12 years and when I'm playing a song, it honestly feels like ecstasy.

Music is great because you can express whatever you're feeling - be it sadness from having a fight with someone you love, joy, anger... Once you grab your instrument and play your heart out you're able to let go of all your emotions, much better than therapy, talking or whatever else. It's at once great exercise for your body, heart and mind. I strongly believe everyone should learn an instrument in their lifetime and it's never too late to start.

Besides, having something creative to do for yourself when you have that extra energy to spend beats the crap out of mindlessly consuming TV. movies, games and whatever other passive entertainment. I'm not saying that playing games can't be creative or that a guitar is always better than therapy but music is certainly something you're missing out on if you're not a player and probably the most beneficial skill one can have if you're counting how many levels it works on.

I wish I could say "because I'm drowning in women," but that has yet to happen as a guitarist. It is fun to play, and gets more fun the better I get. I can't really explain the feeling when you can finally play something like Cliffs of Dover or Eruption.

My hobby is conducting thought expiriments and writing..

It keeps my mind sharp, helps me cultivate my imagination, helps me work though mental distress or anxiety, and one hobby feeds the other.

Playing didgeridoo - I know how to circular breathe, which definitely makes or breaks whether one can play the didgeridoo. Plus it's just kinda calming to drone on it, and pump out any beats that come to mind. Plus it's kinda unique, ya know?

Making fireworks - this one started with me taking them apart YEARS ago. But recently, there was a class I took which taught me how to build commercial-grade firework shells. I knew of what metals and salts produce what colors, but after this class, I gained a whole new appreciation for the process. Building my own stars for shells, making sure it breaks properly, it's just so much fun! Plus there's something calming about holding a 5 inch shell, and knowing fully well that it can kill you if something were to go wrong.

I like roleplaying games (tabletop mostly) and programming. Both share a lot of qualities: they are creative hobbies in which you build something (a program or a story), have sets of rules that can seem to be boring/hard but actually force you to work in your problem solving inside them (besides they are always there for a good reason), require you to work with a community (your gaming group for tabletop RPGs or people who made the language or libraries for programming).,,

Both are pretty awesome on their own too - programming lets you command a computer to do pretty much anything, from creating games to crawling data on the WWW and tabletop gaming is absolutely the most entertaining thing you can do in a group. I'm somewhat of a funny guy and have some pretty funny friends and hilarious stories to tell but I've never laughed as much as when playing RPGs, even if the module/adventure/story we were playing was not comical, it's just so much fun!

I love playing guitar and listening to/recording music (in a very amateur capacity). I just think its really fun to learn to play difficult songs, and to write things that sound cool. I also get a really good feeling that I 'created something' when I finish recording and mixing a song.

I love lifting weights and running because I like being healthy, and it feels really good to make progress, lift more, run faster, etc. After running a long distance I always feel very refreshed, and the pump after lifting is addictive.

Billiards. I love it because it's a great combination of skill and strategy. And the more skillful you get, the more creative you can get with your strategy. Also it's socially acceptable to get drunk while you play. You can also converse during a match. So there's the social aspect of it as well.
